title: k8s-node-pressure-cni-etcd-incident-review-draft
content:
Summary:

This is a working draft for the Feb 24-25 2026 multi-cluster degradation incident. Primary user-visible symptom: intermittent 503s and pod scheduling failures for customer-facing services in eu-central-1 and us-west-2 for ~3 hours. Impact was higher for bursty workloads that allocate short-lived pods (job/cron style) and for real-time inference endpoints with autoscaling.

High-level timeline (rough):
- 2026-02-24 22:03 UTC: First pager hits — elevated 5xx and failed CreateContainerError events observed on several deployments.
- 2026-02-24 22:10 UTC: SREs confirm scheduling backlog (Pending->ContainerCreating delays) and spike in node pressure evictions.
- 2026-02-24 22:22 UTC: Calico CNI reports flapping IPAM allocation errors on multiple nodes in eu-central-1; BGP sessions were stable.
- 2026-02-24 22:35 UTC: etcd leader election flaps observed on control-plane nodes in the affected region; etcd latencies spike (writes 200ms -> 5s).
- 2026-02-24 22:40 UTC: Autoscaler fails to provision new nodes due to cloud API throttling + kubelet registration timeouts; scheduler backlog grows.
- 2026-02-24 23:15 UTC: Emergency mitigation: scale down low-priority batch queues, cordon and drain the most-affected nodes, apply IPAM config temporary increase.
- 2026-02-25 01:00 UTC: Control-plane stabilized after rolling restart of one etcd pod and forcing lease renewals; scheduling backlog clears over next hour.
- 2026-02-25 02:30 UTC: Post-incident triage begins.

Root cause (probable, multi-factor):
1) CNI IPAM exhaustion on a subset of nodes: a combination of rapid pod churn by batch workloads + fragmented IP allocation pools (small host-local ranges) led to transient exhaustion. Calico logged "no IPs available for node" and temporarily marked endpoints NotReady. Our calico-ipam config used /29 host-local pools on these nodes due to a prior manual override from Nov 2025.
2) etcd leader election flaps were triggered by increased control-plane load and ephemeral disk IO spikes on one master node. The IO pressure caused etcd to miss heartbeats and trigger elections; when an election happened, the kube-apiserver experienced short elevated latencies which amplified scheduling delays.
3) Autoscaler + cloud API rate limits: when the scheduler queued many pending pods, Cluster Autoscaler attempted scaling events but hit provider API throttling and node registration timeouts — new nodes either arrived late or failed to register before kubelet eviction thresholds moved workloads.
4) Kubelet eviction contention: nodes experiencing kubelet OOM/kube-proxy churn applied eviction pressure and triggered PodDisruption; some PVCs were detached/re-attached leading to more latency and backlog.

Contributing factors (organizational & config):
- Manual IPAM overrides from Nov 2025 that left some node pools using small host-local ranges (low available IPs).
- Alerts were noisy for a prior CPU/IO transient and had been adjusted down in Dec 2025; the SRE team missed earlier soft signals because thresholds were tuned to reduce noise.
- No circuit-breaker for autoscaler after repeated provider API 429 responses; autoscaler retried and queued requests, making eventual scale attempts take longer.

Evidence (selected logs & commands):
- Calico logs (node kube-flap-03):
  "Feb 24 22:21:15 calico-ipam ERROR: No free addresses for pool host-local-10.240.8.0/29 (node kube-flap-03)"
- etcd metrics (control-plane-1):
  "etcd_request_duration_seconds{type=write} p95=4.6s at 2026-02-24T22:25:00Z"
- Kubelet events: Pod my-batch-job: "Failed to allocate network: ipam: no addresses available" followed by "Pod triggered eviction: node low on memory"
- Cloud provider API responses: a flurry of 429/Throttling for compute.instances.create between 22:30-22:50 UTC in us-west-2 region.

Mitigations performed during incident (ordered):
- Short-term: increased Calico host-local pool size via dynamic update for affected node pools (+ /29 -> /27) which gave immediate breathing room.
- Cordon+drain of ~6 nodes with high fragmentation and IO; replaced with fresh nodes from a control pool with standard IPAM.
- Restarted etcd on control-plane-2 after snapshotting membership and verifying WAL integrity; applied temporary tick-interval tuning to be more tolerant of IO jitter (see risky_notes).
- Rate-limit fallback on autoscaler: we patched CA to back off faster on 429s and added an emergency override to prefer scaling smaller instances where available.

Post-incident actions (next steps / action items):
- Short-term (<=2 weeks):
  * Reconcile IPAM host-local pool sizes across all node pools; remove ad-hoc /29 overrides. Owner: Claire H. ETA: 2026-03-05.
  * Add alert for calico_ipam_alloc_failures > 0 sustained for 5m (currently absent). Owner: Marco R. ETA: 2026-03-03.
  * Add autoscaler behavior tests that simulate cloud API 429s. Owner: SRE infra team. ETA: 2026-03-12.
  * Run cluster-wide etcd IO stress tests in canary clusters to validate tick/heartbeat settings. Owner: Rajesh M. ETA: 2026-03-18.
- Medium-term (<=90 days):
  * Move to centralized IPAM pools for new nodepools and phasing out host-local where feasible. Product/Networking design doc. Owner: Networking team + SRE. ETA: 2026-05-22.
  * Implement autoscaler circuit-breaker that stops retrying on sustained 429s and triggers an ops page. Owner: infra-autoscale. ETA: 2026-04-30.
  * Improve control-plane IO observability: disk IO sagging, WAL stalls, etcd slow ops. Add alert on etcd_request_duration_seconds p95 > 2s. Owner: eng-observability. ETA: 2026-03-15.
- Long-term (>90 days):
  * Re-evaluate CNI choices and IPAM strategy for bursty autoscaling workloads (proof-of-concept for secondary CNI with ENI/host-networking for short-lived pods).
  * Define documented SLO-backed capacity planning for bursty job workloads and autoscaler budgeting.

Runbook draft snippets (to be integrated into SRE runbooks):
- If calico-ipam errors observed:
  1) Check calico node-status and ipam logs: kubectl -n kube-system logs ds/calico-node -l calico-node
  2) Identify node pools with host-local pool size < /26: kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=
  3) Apply emergency pool increase (example): calicoctl create -f - <<EOF
     apiVersion: projectcalico.org/v3
     kind: IPPool
     metadata:
       name: emergency-expand-<nodepool>
     spec:
       cidr: 10.240.8.0/21
       ipipMode: Never
       natOutgoing: true
     EOF
  4) Cordon + drain heavily fragmented nodes. Re-provision with standard pool config.
- If etcd leader flaps and p95 write > 2s:
  1) Check etcd metrics and disk IO: kubectl -n kube-system exec -it etcd-<pod> -- sh -c "iostat -x 1 3"
  2) If IO is saturated, cordon scheduling to this control-plane AZ (use maintenance mode) and force a single-member restart after snapshotting.
  3) If WAL shows corruption, follow safe-recovery SOP (Confluence link in linked_artifacts).
- If Cluster Autoscaler gets repeated 429s:
  1) Pause autoscaler (scale-down disabled) and open a provider support ticket if throttle persists.
  2) Fallback: manually request instance launches in small batches and prefer on-demand if spot/cheap types failing.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did one control-plane node show IO spikes? Hypothesis: background snapshot backup job overlapped with etcd compaction; need to correlate backup times.
- Are there any customers who saw stateful-storage corruption? Early review suggests PVC detaches were transient; run check on PVC attach logs for critical customers. Owner: Sofia A. ETA: 2026-03-04.
- Should we ban host-local IPAM for new clusters? Tradeoffs exist for latency and performance. Need design meeting with Networking and Platform.

Notes to self / SRE war-room shorthand (informal):
- We should avoid changing etcd tick values in prod long-term; the temp tweak was a band-aid. Consider adding IO budget QoS for control-plane VMs.
- Autoscaler backoff change: test thoroughly in staging; small change pushed during incident helped but needs hardening.
- Keep incident timeline concise for execs: focus on multi-factor nature, immediate mitigations, and clear next actions.

Appendix (useful commands & snippets):
- Check calico IPAM counters: calicoctl get ippool -o wide
- Inspect etcd metrics via metrics server: curl -s http://controlplane-metrics:2379/metrics | grep etcd_request_duration_seconds
- Pending pod diagnostics: kubectl get events --all-namespaces --sort-by=.metadata.creationTimestamp | tail -n 200 | grep -E "FailedScheduling|FailedCreate|ipam|attachvolume"

Slack references: #sre-incidents thread (message ids): 84901..84947; primary incident page pinned in #oncall-ops.

Draft notes for the postmortem write-up (to be refined for execs):
- TL;DR: transient IPAM exhaustion + etcd IO-induced leader flaps + autoscaler/provisioning latency combined to create a severe but remediable scheduling outage. No confirmed data loss.
- Customer impact: 503s, increased tail latency, some job failures; estimated 2.8k failing requests across affected regions.
- Root cause summary and actions: reconcile IPAM, improve autoscaler circuit-breakers, increase etcd IO observability and run canary tests.

Status: still in draft. Please add notes inline and escalate any counter-evidence.
